key_insight: CARS anchors attention to coronary centerlines to predict pressure and velocity at arbitrary lumen points, reducing geometry-fusion cost from O(N²) to O(N n_f).
engineering_relevance: The surrogate evaluates a coronary flow case in 87 ms versus 572–1,063 s for CFD, supporting rapid pressure-based assessment.
method: Inputs: image-derived centerline, per-point lumen radius, and scalar inlet flow rate.
Uses the case’s own centerline as the attention focal set to encode geometry.
Learns steady incompressible Navier–Stokes solution maps from OpenFOAM simulations, with separate models per coronary territory.
evidence_signal: Trained per territory on 2,700 simulations with synthetic focal lesions, CARS achieved pressure/velocity relative ℓ₂ errors of 0.120/0.149 (left) and 0.063/0.119 (right), with 97.7%/96.3% agreement on the CFD-derived FFR ≤ 0.8 decision.
watch_item: Predicted velocity does not satisfy continuity closely enough for derived quantities, and territory-specific weights limit model reuse.
paper_title: CARS: a centerline-anchored attention surrogate for coronary blood flow on skeleton-generated lumen geometries
